```yaml
# ARM A. BPT's own notation, bpt/v1, exactly as docs/CONTRACT-FORMAT.md specifies.
#
# This is packages/contracts/product/list/contract.yaml with one addition, made
# to every arm equally: the price-exact rule. Arm A states money semantics twice
# (through `type: money` and through the rule) while the other arms state it once
# (through the rule alone). Without that rule the arms would not carry the same
# information, and the comparison would be measuring a missing sentence rather
# than a notation.
id: product.list
version: 1
kind: query
title: List products

authorization:
  required: true
  roles: [customer]

input:
  search: { type: text, required: false }
  page:   { type: integer, min: 1, default: 1 }
  size:   { type: integer, min: 1, max: 100, default: 20 }
  minPrice: { type: money, required: false }

output:
  items:
    type: list
    of:
      object:
        id:        { type: text }
        name:      { type: text }
        price:     { type: money }
        currency:  { type: text }
        available: { type: boolean }
  total: { type: integer }
  page:  { type: integer }

rules:
  - id: ordering
    describe: items ordered by name ascending
  - id: search-case-insensitive
    describe: search by name ignores case
  - id: availability
    describe: only available products are returned
  - id: price-exact
    describe: >-
      price is a monetary amount and must round trip without losing precision,
      so it is never held in binary floating point
  - id: price-filter
    describe: when minPrice is given, only products priced at or above it are returned
  - id: currency-code
    describe: currency is the three letter code of the currency the price is in

errors:
  - code: INVALID_PARAMETER
    category: validation
    retryable: false
    when: page or size out of range
  - code: UNAUTHORIZED
    category: user
    retryable: false
    when: session missing or expired
```
